purpose: Adjudicate high-recall, cross-paper node candidates while preserving exact sentence-level provenance.

decisions.accept: The grounded span denotes a clear standalone entity or scientifically useful broad concept, fits one ontology class, and has a specific sentence ID.
decisions.review: The grounded span may be useful but its boundary, ontology class, or identity remains genuinely ambiguous and requires a human decision.
decisions.reject: The candidate lacks sentence traceability, remains vague after attempted resolution, is malformed, unsupported, or cannot function as a graph node.

criteria.question: Does the candidate surface text occur at the supplied exact offsets?
Does the candidate point to one specific, non-empty sentence ID containing its exact evidence span?
Does the span name a clear entity or scientifically useful concept, including a broad concept when it can stand alone?
Can the candidate be assigned to one existing ontology class supported by the evidence?
Can a concise, unambiguous canonical name be stated or mapped to one same-type prior node without inventing information?

hard_constraints: Never invent or move a source span.
Reject every candidate whose source has no specific non-empty sentence ID.
Reject a vague or unclear candidate unless adjudication resolves it to one specific, evidence-grounded canonical node.
Broad scientific and cross-domain concepts qualify when they are clear, useful, grounded, and ontology-compatible.
Do not require the node to be central to the current paper; related-work and cross-paper concepts may be retained.
Automatically map only an exact canonical-name match among supplied prior nodes of the same ontology type.
Do not create relationships during node adjudication.
Use review for a grounded candidate requiring a human boundary, type, or identity choice; use reject when its identity remains vague.
